title: Maximality of the Došen–Petrić Boolean Category
abstract: Categorical proof theory expresses identifications of proofs as equations between arrows. We prove that the zero-identity Boolean category of Došen and Petrić, freely generated by a nonempty set of propositional variables, is maximal. Adjoining an equation between distinct arrows with the same source and target, and closing under the arrow operations and uniform formula substitution, identifies all parallel arrows. This disproves their conjecture in Section 14.2 of the September 2007 revision of Proof-Theoretical Coherence. The proof uses Boolean Coherence to select a pair of variable occurrences on which the two arrows differ. Composition with arrows selecting these occurrences, uniform substitution and two isomorphisms yield equality of the product projections. We also prove that any zero-identity Boolean category satisfying such an additional equation under every interpretation of the variables has at most one arrow between any two objects. The Lean formalization proves coherence, maximality and this model corollary for the category presented by the defining equations. It also establishes the correspondence between substitution on tagged occurrence sets and substitution on finite ordinals.
